title: IIT JAM 2027 Chemistry (CY) — Full Length Mock Test 03
titleEn: IIT JAM 2027 Chemistry (CY) — Full Length Mock Test 03

questions.questionTextEn: Which reagent selectively oxidizes $(E)$-but-2-en-1-ol to $(E)$-but-2-enal without over-oxidizing to the carboxylic acid or cleaving the double bond?
questions.explanationEn: Activated $\text{MnO}_2$ is a mild, chemoselective oxidant specifically suited for oxidizing allylic and benzylic alcohols to $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated aldehydes or ketones without affecting the $\text{C}=\text{C}$ bond or over-oxidizing to carboxylic acids. Jones reagent oxidizes primary alcohols to carboxylic acids, hot $\text{KMnO}_4$ cleaves alkenes, and $\text{OsO}_4$ performs dihydroxylation. Hence, option **(C)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: The total number of normal modes of vibration in an acetylene ($\text{H}-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\text{H}$) molecule is
questions.explanationEn: Acetylene ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_2$) is a linear molecule with $N = 4$ atoms. The number of vibrational degrees of freedom for a linear polyatomic molecule is $3N - 5 = 3(4) - 5 = 7$.

questions.questionTextEn: According to the radius ratio rule for ionic solids, if the cation-to-anion radius ratio ($r_+/r_-$) lies between $0.414$ and $0.732$, the expected coordination number and coordination geometry of the cation are
questions.explanationEn: The limiting radius ratios are: $0.155\text{--}0.225$ (trigonal planar, $\text{CN}=3$), $0.225\text{--}0.414$ (tetrahedral, $\text{CN}=4$), $0.414\text{--}0.732$ (octahedral, $\text{CN}=6$), and $0.732\text{--}1.000$ (cubic, $\text{CN}=8$).

questions.questionTextEn: For a reversible galvanic cell operating at constant pressure, the temperature coefficient of standard EMF, $\left(\frac{\partial E^\circ}{\partial T}\right)_P$, is found to be negative. This implies that for the cell reaction,
questions.explanationEn: Since $\Delta S^\circ = nF\left(\frac{\partial E^\circ}{\partial T}\right)_P$, a negative temperature coefficient gives $\Delta S^\circ < 0$. From $\Delta H^\circ = \Delta G^\circ + T\Delta S^\circ$, having $T\Delta S^\circ < 0$ implies $\Delta H^\circ < \Delta G^\circ$ (more negative enthalpy than Gibbs energy).

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following compounds gives a **positive** iodoform test ($\text{I}_2/\text{NaOH}$, yellow precipitate of $\text{CHI}_3$)?
questions.explanationEn: The iodoform test is positive for methyl ketones ($\text{RCOCH}_3$), acetaldehyde, ethanol, and secondary methyl carbinols ($\text{RCH(OH)CH}_3$). Pentan-2-ol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$) is oxidized in situ to pentan-2-one and gives yellow $\text{CHI}_3$.

questions.questionTextEn: Heating 2-bromo-2-methylbutane with potassium *tert*-butoxide ($t\text{-BuOK}$) in *tert*-butanol gives as the major alkene product
questions.explanationEn: With a sterically bulky strong base such as $t\text{-BuOK}$, E2 elimination of a tertiary alkyl halide occurs preferentially by abstracting the less sterically hindered primary $\beta$-hydrogen rather than the more hindered secondary $\beta$-hydrogen. This affords the **Hofmann (less substituted) alkene**, 2-methylbut-1-ene, as the major product. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: In the X-ray powder diffraction pattern of a body-centered cubic (bcc) crystal, which of the following reflections $(hkl)$ is **systematically absent** (forbidden)?
questions.explanationEn: For a bcc lattice, reflections are observed only when $h + k + l$ is **even**. Checking the sums: $(110) \to 2$ (even), $(200) \to 2$ (even), $(211) \to 4$ (even), and $(210) \to 3$ (odd, systematically absent).

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following substituents on a benzene ring is **deactivating** yet ***ortho*/*para*-directing** in electrophilic aromatic substitution ($\text{S}_\text{E}\text{Ar}$)?
questions.explanationEn: Halogens such as $-\text{Cl}$ deactivate the ring inductively ($-I > +M$), slowing $\text{S}_\text{E}\text{Ar}$ relative to benzene, but donate lone-pair electron density by resonance ($+M$) into the *ortho* and *para* positions of the Wheland intermediate, making them *ortho*/*para*-directors. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: The tetrahedral complex $[\text{CoCl}_4]^{2-}$ is intensely blue ($\varepsilon \approx 600\text{ L mol}^{-1}\text{ cm}^{-1}$), whereas the octahedral complex $[\text{Co(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+}$ is pale pink ($\varepsilon \approx 10\text{ L mol}^{-1}\text{ cm}^{-1}$). The much higher absorption intensity of $[\text{CoCl}_4]^{2-}$ is primarily due to
optionsEn: absence of a center of inversion in tetrahedral geometry, which allows $d\text{--}p$ orbital mixing and relaxes the Laporte selection rule
a ligand-to-metal charge transfer band in the visible region for $[\text{CoCl}_4]^{2-}$
questions.explanationEn: Both complexes have spin-allowed $d\text{--}d$ transitions ($^4A_2 \to {}^4T_1(P)$ in $T_d$ and $^4T_{1g}(F) \to {}^4T_{1g}(P)$ in $O_h$). Because a tetrahedron lacks an inversion center ($i$), the $t_2$ $d$-orbitals mix with $t_2$ $p$-orbitals, partially relaxing the Laporte rule and increasing $\varepsilon$ by roughly two orders of magnitude.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following molecules is **rotational (microwave) active**?
questions.explanationEn: A molecule must possess a permanent electric dipole moment to exhibit a pure rotational (microwave) spectrum. $\text{CO}_2$ (linear symmetric), $\text{CH}_4$ ($T_d$), and $\text{SF}_6$ ($O_h$) have zero dipole moment, whereas linear unsymmetrical $\text{N}_2\text{O}$ ($\text{N}-\text{N}-\text{O}$) has a permanent dipole moment and is microwave active.

questions.questionTextEn: Given the trans-effect order $\text{Cl}^- > \text{NH}_3$, the selective synthesis of *cis*-$[\text{Pt(NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$ (cisplatin) and *trans*-$[\text{Pt(NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$, respectively, is best achieved by
optionsEn: treating $[\text{PtCl}_4]^{2-}$ with $2\text{ NH}_3$ (for *cis*) and treating $[\text{Pt(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$ with $2\text{ Cl}^-$ (for *trans*)
treating $[\text{Pt(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$ with $2\text{ Cl}^-$ (for *cis*) and treating $[\text{PtCl}_4]^{2-}$ with $2\text{ NH}_3$ (for *trans*)
treating $[\text{PtCl}_4]^{2-}$ with $2\text{ NH}_3$ for both isomers at different temperatures
treating $[\text{Pt(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$ with $2\text{ Cl}^-$ in the presence of $\text{Ag}^+$ for *cis*
questions.explanationEn: From $[\text{PtCl}_4]^{2-}$, the first $\text{NH}_3$ gives $[\text{PtCl}_3(\text{NH}_3)]^-$. Because $\text{Cl}^-$ has a stronger trans effect than $\text{NH}_3$, a $\text{Cl}^-$ trans to $\text{Cl}^-$ is labilized and replaced by the second $\text{NH}_3$, giving *cis*-$[\text{Pt(NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$. Conversely, from $[\text{Pt(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$, the first $\text{Cl}^-$ enters to give $[\text{Pt(NH}_3)_3\text{Cl}]^+$, and that $\text{Cl}^-$ directs the second $\text{Cl}^-$ trans to itself, yielding *trans*-$[\text{Pt(NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$.

questions.questionTextEn: The plot of nuclear binding energy per nucleon ($\text{BE}/A$) versus mass number ($A$) reaches a broad maximum of $\approx 8.8\text{ MeV}$ near $A \approx 56$ ($^{56}\text{Fe}$/$^{62}\text{Ni}$). Consequently, energy is **released** during
optionsEn: fusion of very heavy nuclei ($A > 200$) and fission of very light nuclei ($A < 20$)
fusion of very light nuclei ($A < 20$) and fission of very heavy nuclei ($A > 200$)
neither fusion nor fission of any nuclei
questions.explanationEn: Both fusing light nuclei ($A < 56$) toward heavier nuclei and splitting heavy nuclei ($A > 56$, e.g. $^{235}\text{U}$) into medium-mass fragments move products toward the maximum of the $\text{BE}/A$ curve near $A \approx 56$, increasing total binding energy and releasing nuclear energy.

questions.questionTextEn: Which protecting group is selectively removed under mild **basic** conditions (using $20\%$ piperidine in DMF) during solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS)?
questions.explanationEn: The **Fmoc** group has an acidic $9$-fluorenyl proton that undergoes rapid $\text{E1cb}$ $\beta$-elimination upon treatment with mild secondary amine base (**piperidine** in DMF), releasing dibenzofulvene and $\text{CO}_2$. By contrast, **Boc** is acid-labile (TFA) and **Cbz/Bn** are removed by catalytic hydrogenolysis ($\text{H}_2/\text{Pd-C}$). Hence, option **(C)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn:
For the electrolyte concentration cell **with transference** reversible to the anion:
$\text{Ag}(s)\,|\,\text{AgCl}(s)\,|\,\text{HCl}(a_1)\,:\,\text{HCl}(a_2)\,|\,\text{AgCl}(s)\,|\,\text{Ag}(s)$
the cell EMF $E_t$ (assuming constant cation transport number $t_+$) is given by
questions.explanationEn: When the electrodes are reversible to the anion ($\text{Cl}^-$), passing $1\text{ F}$ transfers $t_+$ moles of $\text{HCl}$ from activity $a_1$ to $a_2$ (with $a_{\text{HCl}} = a_\pm^2$). Hence $E_t = -\frac{\Delta G}{F} = \frac{t_+ RT}{F}\ln\left(\frac{a_{\pm,1}^2}{a_{\pm,2}^2}\right) = \frac{2 t_+ RT}{F}\ln\left(\frac{a_{\pm,1}}{a_{\pm,2}}\right)$.

questions.questionTextEn: During the electrolytic refining of blister copper using an impure copper anode, a pure copper cathode, and acidified $\text{CuSO}_4$ electrolyte, which of the following sets of metallic impurities collects as **anode mud**?
questions.explanationEn: More electropositive (active) impurities such as $\text{Fe}$, $\text{Zn}$, and $\text{Ni}$ oxidize into the $\text{CuSO}_4$ solution as ions and remain dissolved. Less electropositive (noble) metals such as $\text{Ag}$, $\text{Au}$, and $\text{Pt}$ are not oxidized at the operating anode potential and fall to the bottom as valuable anode mud.

questions.questionTextEn: Assuming complete dissociation, the freezing point of a $0.10\text{ mol kg}^{-1}$ aqueous solution of $\text{K}_2\text{SO}_4$ ($K_f = 1.86\text{ K kg mol}^{-1}$) is
questions.explanationEn: Complete dissociation $\text{K}_2\text{SO}_4 \to 2\text{K}^+ + \text{SO}_4^{2-}$ gives $i = 3$. Thus $\Delta T_f = i K_f m = 3 \times 1.86 \times 0.10 = 0.558\text{ K}$, so $T_f = -0.558\,^\circ\text{C}$.

questions.questionTextEn: Chemoselective reduction of ethyl 4-oxopentanoate ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{Et}$) with $\text{NaBH}_4$ in ethanol at $0\,^\circ\text{C}$ followed by acidic workup gives
questions.explanationEn: $\text{NaBH}_4$ is a mild hydride reducing agent that rapidly reduces aldehydes and ketones to alcohols, while leaving less electrophilic esters completely untouched at $0\,^\circ\text{C}$. Thus, the ketone at C4 is reduced to a secondary alcohol, yielding **ethyl 4-hydroxypentanoate**. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: In **cholesterol** ($\text{C}_{27}\text{H}_{46}\text{O}$), the single double bond is located at $\text{C5}=\text{C6}$, the secondary hydroxyl group at $\text{C3}$ is $\beta$ (equatorial), and the two angular methyl groups at $\text{C10}$ and $\text{C13}$ are both $\beta$ (axial). What is the stereochemistry of the **B/C** and **C/D** ring junctions in cholesterol?
optionsEn: Both B/C and C/D ring junctions are *cis*
Both B/C and C/D ring junctions are *trans*
questions.explanationEn: In cholesterol (and nearly all natural steroids), the **B/C** ($8\beta\text{-H}, 9\alpha\text{-H}$) and **C/D** ($13\beta\text{-Me}, 14\alpha\text{-H}$) ring junctions are **both *trans*-fused**, giving the steroid nucleus its characteristic rigid, flat, extended conformation. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: A spherical liquid drop of radius $R$ and surface tension $\gamma$ is sprayed isothermally into $8$ identical smaller spherical droplets. The minimum work required for this process is
questions.explanationEn: By volume conservation, $\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = 8 \times \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 \implies r = R/2$. The surface area increases from $A_1 = 4\pi R^2$ to $A_2 = 8(4\pi r^2) = 8\pi R^2$, so $\Delta A = 4\pi R^2$ and $W = \gamma\Delta A = 4\pi R^2\gamma$.

questions.questionTextEn: A quantum system has orthonormal energy eigenstates $\phi_1, \phi_2, \phi_3$ with eigenvalues $E_1 = E_0$, $E_2 = 4E_0$, and $E_3 = 9E_0$. If the system is prepared in the normalized state $\Psi = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{14}}(\phi_1 + 2\phi_2 - 3\phi_3)$, the expectation value of energy $\langle E \rangle$ is
questions.explanationEn: The probabilities of measuring $E_1, E_2, E_3$ are $|c_1|^2 = \frac{1}{14}$, $|c_2|^2 = \frac{4}{14}$, and $|c_3|^2 = \frac{9}{14}$. Therefore, $\langle E \rangle = \frac{1(1) + 4(4) + 9(9)}{14}E_0 = \frac{1 + 16 + 81}{14}E_0 = \frac{98}{14}E_0 = 7E_0$.

questions.questionTextEn: The correct decreasing order of basicity of $\text{NH}_3$, $\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2$, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{NH}$, and $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{N}$ in **aqueous solution** is
questions.explanationEn: In water, basicity reflects a balance between $+I$ stabilization (favoring more methyl groups) and hydration of the conjugate ammonium ion via $\text{N}^+\text{–H}\cdots\text{OH}_2$ hydrogen bonds (favoring fewer methyl groups). For methylamines, hydration dominates over $+I$ for the tertiary amine, giving $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{NH}$ ($\text{p}K_{aH} = 10.73$) $>$ $\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2$ ($10.66$) $>$ $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{N}$ ($9.80$) $>$ $\text{NH}_3$ ($9.25$).

questions.questionTextEn: For a unimolecular reaction following the Lindemann–Hinshelwood mechanism, a plot of $1/k_{\text{uni}}$ against $1/[M]$ gives a straight line with slope $2.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol dm}^{-3}\text{ s}$ and $y$-intercept $5.0\text{ s}$. The concentration $[M]_{1/2}$ at which $k_{\text{uni}}$ drops to half of its high-pressure limiting value $k_\infty$ is
questions.explanationEn: From $\frac{1}{k_{\text{uni}}} = \frac{k_{-1}}{k_1 k_2} + \frac{1}{k_1 [M]} = \frac{1}{k_\infty} + \frac{1}{k_1 [M]}$, we have intercept $= 1/k_\infty = 5.0\text{ s}$ and slope $= 1/k_1 = 2.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol dm}^{-3}\text{ s}$. When $k_{\text{uni}} = k_\infty/2$, $\frac{1}{k_{\text{uni}}} = \frac{2}{k_\infty}$, so $\frac{1}{k_1 [M]_{1/2}} = \frac{1}{k_\infty} \implies [M]_{1/2} = \frac{\text{slope}}{\text{intercept}} = \frac{2.0 \times 10^{-3}}{5.0} = 4.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$.

questions.questionTextEn: An isomer of $\text{C}_6\text{H}_4\text{Cl}_2$ shows exactly **one** sharp singlet in its $^1\text{H}$ NMR spectrum and **two** signals in its $^{13}\text{C}$ NMR spectrum. The isomer is
questions.explanationEn: 1,4-Dichlorobenzene has $D_{2h}$ symmetry: all $4$ aromatic protons are equivalent ($1$ $^1\text{H}$ singlet), and there are only $2$ types of carbons (C1/C4 bearing $\text{Cl}$, and C2/C3/C5/C6 bearing $\text{H}$). By contrast, 1,2-dichlorobenzene has $3$ $^{13}\text{C}$ signals and 1,3-dichlorobenzene has $4$ $^{13}\text{C}$ signals.

questions.questionTextEn: For an electron in a $3d$ orbital with magnetic quantum number $m_l = -1$, the magnitude of orbital angular momentum $|\vec{L}|$ and its $z$-component $L_z$, respectively, are
questions.explanationEn: For a $d$-orbital, $l = 2$, so $|\vec{L}| = \sqrt{l(l+1)}\hbar = \sqrt{2(3)}\hbar = \sqrt{6}\hbar$. With $m_l = -1$, $L_z = m_l\hbar = -\hbar$.

questions.questionTextEn: Heating 2-methylcyclohexane-1,3-dione with methyl vinyl ketone (but-3-en-2-one) in the presence of a catalytic base yields the bicyclic enone
questions.explanationEn: 2-Methylcyclohexane-1,3-dione undergoes **Michael addition** to methyl vinyl ketone at C2 to form the triketone 2-methyl-2-(3-oxobutyl)cyclohexane-1,3-dione, followed by intramolecular **aldol condensation** (dehydration) to form the classic **Wieland–Miescher ketone**, 8a-methyl-3,4,8,8a-tetrahydronaphthalene-1,6(2$H$,7$H$)-dione. Hence, option **(A)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: In carborane cluster electron counting, a $\text{CH}$ vertex is isolobal and isoelectronic with a $\text{BH}^-$ vertex (contributing $3$ skeletal electrons). Accordingly, the dicarborane $\text{C}_2\text{B}_{10}\text{H}_{12}$ has
optionsEn: $12$ skeletal electron pairs and a *nido* structure
$13$ skeletal electron pairs and a *closo* icosahedral structure
$14$ skeletal electron pairs and a *nido* structure
$13$ skeletal electron pairs and an *arachno* structure
questions.explanationEn: In $\text{C}_2\text{B}_{10}\text{H}_{12}$, total vertices $n = 2 + 10 = 12$. Skeletal electrons $= 2(3) + 10(2) = 26$, which is $13 = n + 1$ skeletal electron pairs (isoelectronic with $[\text{B}_{12}\text{H}_{12}]^{2-}$). Hence it adopts a *closo* icosahedral structure.

questions.questionTextEn: The population variance $\sigma^2 = \dfrac{1}{N}\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{N}(x_i - \bar{x})^2$ of the data set $\{2, 4, 6, 8, 10\}$ is

Solvolysis of *anti*-7-norbornenyl tosylate in acetic acid is approximately $10^{11}$ times faster than that of saturated 7-norbornyl tosylate, and proceeds with complete retention of configuration at C7. This dramatic rate enhancement and stereochemical outcome are due to
optionsEn: steric relief of the bicyclic bridge in an $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ transition state
$\pi$-bond neighboring group participation (anchimeric assistance) forming a symmetrical non-classical bridged carbocation
direct backside $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ attack by acetic acid
E2 elimination followed by *syn* addition of acetic acid
questions.explanationEn: In *anti*-7-norbornenyl tosylate, the $\text{C2}=\text{C3}$ $\pi$-bond is ideally aligned backside ($180^\circ$) to the departing $\text{C7}-\text{OTs}$ bond. It participates intramolecularly (**anchimeric assistance**) to expel $-\text{OTs}$ and form a symmetrical non-classical bishomoaromatic carbocation, accelerating solvolysis by $10^{11}$. Because the $\pi$-cloud shields the *syn* face, $\text{AcOH}$ attacks exclusively from the *anti* face, giving **100% retention of configuration**. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: At $298\text{ K}$, $E^\circ(\text{Ag}^+/\text{Ag}) = +0.799\text{ V}$ and $E^\circ(\text{AgCl}/\text{Ag},\text{Cl}^-) = +0.222\text{ V}$. Taking $\frac{2.303RT}{F} = 0.0591\text{ V}$, $\log_{10} K_{sp}$ of $\text{AgCl}$ at $298\text{ K}$ is closest to
questions.explanationEn: Combining $\text{Ag}(s) \to \text{Ag}^+ + e^-$ ($-0.799\text{ V}$) and $\text{AgCl}(s) + e^- \to \text{Ag}(s) + \text{Cl}^-$ ($+0.222\text{ V}$) gives $\text{AgCl}(s) \rightleftharpoons \text{Ag}^+ + \text{Cl}^-$ with $E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = 0.222 - 0.799 = -0.577\text{ V}$. Thus $\log_{10} K_{sp} = \frac{n E^\circ_{\text{cell}}}{0.0591} = \frac{-0.577}{0.0591} = -9.76$.

questions.questionTextEn: In the molecular orbital diagram of $\text{HF}$ (with the internuclear axis along $z$), the $2p_x$ and $2p_y$ orbitals of fluorine
optionsEn: form degenerate $\pi$ bonding orbitals with the $1s$ orbital of hydrogen
remain strictly non-bonding because they have $\pi$ symmetry and zero net overlap with the $\sigma$-symmetric $\text{H}\,1s$ orbital
mix strongly with the $\text{F}\,2s$ orbital to form $\sigma^*$ orbitals
lie lower in energy than the $\text{F}\,2s$ orbital
questions.explanationEn: In $\text{HF}$ ($C_{\infty v}$), the $\text{H}\,1s$ orbital has $\sigma$ symmetry and can only overlap with $\text{F}\,2p_z$ (and weakly with $\text{F}\,2s$). The $\text{F}\,2p_x$ and $2p_y$ orbitals have $\pi$ symmetry, giving zero net overlap with $\text{H}\,1s$, so they remain degenerate non-bonding ($1\pi$) lone pairs on $\text{F}$.

questions.questionTextEn: Regarding the pure rotational (microwave) spectrum of a diatomic molecule, the correct statement(s) is/are
optionsEn: For a rigid rotor, adjacent absorption lines are equally spaced by $2B$.
Including centrifugal distortion causes the spacing between adjacent lines to decrease at higher $J$.
Homonuclear diatomic molecules like $\text{H}_2$ and $\text{N}_2$ show pure rotational microwave absorption spectra.
Isotopic substitution with a heavier isotope decreases the rotational constant $B$.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) True:** $\tilde{\nu}_{J\to J+1} = 2B(J+1)$, so adjacent lines are separated by $2B$.
- **(B) True:** Centrifugal distortion adds $-4D(J+1)^3$ to the transition wavenumber, compressing line spacing at higher $J$.
- **(C) False:** Homonuclear diatomics lack a permanent dipole moment and are microwave inactive.
- **(D) True:** Increasing reduced mass $\mu$ increases $I = \mu r^2$, decreasing $B \propto 1/I$.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) regarding spinel structures ($\text{AB}_2\text{O}_4$) is/are **CORRECT**?
optionsEn: In a spinel lattice, $\text{O}^{2-}$ ions form a cubic close-packed (ccp/fcc) array with cations occupying $1/8$ of the tetrahedral voids and $1/2$ of the octahedral voids.
$\text{Fe}_3\text{O}_4$ is an inverse spinel formulated as $[\text{Fe}^{3+}]_{\text{tet}}[\text{Fe}^{2+}\text{Fe}^{3+}]_{\text{oct}}\text{O}_4$.
In an inverse spinel, all $\text{A}^{2+}$ cations occupy tetrahedral sites.
questions.explanationEn:
- (A) True: Per $4\,\text{O}^{2-}$ ions there are $8$ tetrahedral voids ($1$ occupied $= 1/8$) and $4$ octahedral voids ($2$ occupied $= 1/2$).
- (B) True: $\text{MgAl}_2\text{O}_4$ is the prototype normal spinel, and $\text{Mn}_3\text{O}_4$ ($\text{Mn}^{2+}$ $d^5$ tet, $\text{Mn}^{3+}$ $d^4$ oct) is a normal spinel.
- (C) True: Magnetite is an inverse spinel.
- (D) False: In an inverse spinel, $\text{A}^{2+}$ occupies *octahedral* sites ($[\text{B}]_{\text{tet}}[\text{AB}]_{\text{oct}}\text{O}_4$).

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about $\alpha$-amino acids and their isoelectric points ($\text{p}I$) is/are correct?
optionsEn: At its isoelectric point, an amino acid exists predominantly as a dipolar zwitterion with zero net electrical charge and minimum aqueous solubility.
For an acidic amino acid such as aspartic acid, $\text{p}I = \frac{1}{2}(\text{p}K_{a1} + \text{p}K_{aR})$ where $\text{p}K_{a1}$ and $\text{p}K_{aR}$ are the two carboxyl $\text{p}K_a$ values.
For a basic amino acid such as lysine, $\text{p}I = \frac{1}{2}(\text{p}K_{a2} + \text{p}K_{aR})$ where $\text{p}K_{a2}$ and $\text{p}K_{aR}$ are the two ammonium $\text{p}K_a$ values.
All 20 standard proteinogenic amino acids have $\text{p}I$ values strictly between $5.0$ and $7.0$.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) Correct:** At $\text{pH} = \text{p}I$, net charge $= 0$, minimizing electrostatic repulsion between molecules and giving minimum solubility.
- **(B) Correct:** For acidic amino acids (Asp, Glu), the neutral zwitterion lies between the two lower (carboxyl) $\text{p}K_a$s.
- **(C) Correct:** For basic amino acids (Lys, Arg, His), the neutral zwitterion lies between the two higher (ammonium/basic side-chain) $\text{p}K_a$s.
- **(D) Incorrect:** Acidic amino acids have $\text{p}I \approx 2.8\text{--}3.2$ and basic amino acids have $\text{p}I \approx 7.6\text{--}10.8$.
Hence, **(A), (B), and (C)** are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: According to Molecular Orbital Theory, which of the following statement(s) is/are **CORRECT**?
optionsEn: Ionization of $\text{N}_2$ to $\text{N}_2^+$ decreases the bond order from $3.0$ to $2.5$ and lengthens the $\text{N}-\text{N}$ bond.
Ionization of $\text{O}_2$ to $\text{O}_2^+$ increases the bond order from $2.0$ to $2.5$ and shortens the $\text{O}-\text{O}$ bond.
$\text{CN}^-$, $\text{CO}$, and $\text{NO}^+$ are isoelectronic and each has a bond order of $3$.
The HOMO of $\text{F}_2$ is a $\sigma_{2p}$ bonding orbital.
questions.explanationEn:
- (A) True: The electron is removed from the bonding $3\sigma_g$ HOMO of $\text{N}_2$, decreasing $\text{BO}$ to $2.5$.
- (B) True: The electron is removed from the antibonding $1\pi_g^*$ HOMO of $\text{O}_2$, increasing $\text{BO}$ to $2.5$.
- (C) True: Each has $14$ total ($10$ valence) electrons and $\text{BO} = 3$.
- (D) False: The HOMO of $\text{F}_2$ ($18\text{ e}^-$) is the antibonding $\pi_{2p}^*$ ($1\pi_g$) orbital.

questions.questionTextEn: For a pure one-component substance ($C = 1$), the correct statement(s) regarding its $P\text{--}T$ phase diagram is/are
optionsEn: In a single-phase region, the system is bivariant ($F = 2$).
Along any two-phase coexistence boundary, the system is univariant ($F = 1$).
The liquid–vapor coexistence curve terminates at the critical point $(T_c, P_c)$.
Four phases of a pure one-component substance can coexist simultaneously in thermodynamic equilibrium.
questions.explanationEn: By the Gibbs phase rule $F = C - P + 2 = 3 - P$: for $P = 1$, $F = 2$; for $P = 2$, $F = 1$; for $P = 3$, $F = 0$. Having $P = 4$ would require $F = -1$, which is impossible (so D is false). Also, the liquid–vapor curve ends at the critical point (C is true).

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) about $^1\text{H}$ NMR spectra is/are correct?
optionsEn: Adding a drop of $\text{D}_2\text{O}$ to an NMR sample causes acidic $-\text{OH}$ and $-\text{NH}$ signals to diminish or disappear.
1,3,5-Trimethylbenzene (mesitylene) exhibits exactly $2$ singlets in its $^1\text{H}$ NMR spectrum with an integration ratio of $3:1$.
Acetone ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$) and *tert*-butyl methyl ether ($(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{COCH}_3$) both show only singlets in their $^1\text{H}$ NMR spectra.
1,2-Dibromoethane ($\text{BrCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$) shows a triplet in its $^1\text{H}$ NMR spectrum.
questions.explanationEn: (A), (B), and (C) are correct (mesitylene has $9\text{H}$ methyls and $3\text{H}$ aryl protons $\implies 3:1$; acetone has 1 singlet, MTBE has 2 singlets). (D) is false because all four protons of $\text{BrCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$ are chemically equivalent and do not split one another, giving a **singlet**.

questions.questionTextEn: Regarding surface tension ($\gamma$) and capillary action of liquids, the correct statement(s) is/are
optionsEn: For most pure liquids, surface tension decreases with increasing temperature and vanishes at the critical temperature $T_c$.
The capillary rise height $h$ of a wetting liquid is inversely proportional to the internal radius $r$ of the capillary tube.
A liquid that wets glass (contact angle $\theta < 90^\circ$) forms a concave meniscus and rises in a glass capillary.
Adding a surfactant to water increases the surface tension of water.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) True:** Thermal agitation weakens cohesive forces; at $T_c$ the liquid–vapor interface disappears ($\gamma = 0$).
- **(B) True:** Jurin's law: $h = \frac{2\gamma\cos\theta}{\rho g r} \propto 1/r$.
- **(C) True:** When $\theta < 90^\circ$, $\cos\theta > 0$, giving capillary rise and a concave meniscus.
- **(D) False:** Surfactants accumulate at the interface and dramatically *lower* surface tension.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following reagent systems cleanly oxidize a primary aliphatic alcohol ($\text{RCH}_2\text{OH}$) to an aldehyde ($\text{RCHO}$) without over-oxidation to the carboxylic acid?
questions.explanationEn: **PCC** in anhydrous $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2$ (A), **Swern oxidation** (B), and **Dess–Martin periodinane** (C) all operate under anhydrous conditions where no aldehyde hydrate forms, stopping cleanly at the aldehyde. Aqueous **Jones reagent** (D) hydrates the aldehyde in situ and over-oxidizes it to the carboxylic acid. Hence, **(A), (B), and (C)** are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Consider the consecutive first-order reaction $A \xrightarrow{k_1} B \xrightarrow{k_2} C$ with $[A]_0 = a$ and $[B]_0 = [C]_0 = 0$. The correct statement(s) is/are
optionsEn: When $k_2 \gg k_1$, the steady-state approximation holds for $B$ after a brief induction period, giving $[B] \approx \frac{k_1}{k_2}[A]$.
When $k_1 \gg k_2$, the rate of formation of $C$ is controlled primarily by $k_2$.
At $t = t_{\max}$, the rate of formation of $C$ is zero.
questions.explanationEn: At $t = t_{\max}$, $\frac{d[B]}{dt} = k_1[A] - k_2[B] = 0 \implies k_1[A] = k_2[B]$ (A true), while $\frac{d[C]}{dt} = k_2[B]_{\max}$ is actually at its **maximum** (D false). When $k_2 \gg k_1$, $B$ decays rapidly so SSA gives $[B] \approx (k_1/k_2)[A]$ (B true). When $k_1 \gg k_2$, $A$ converts quickly to $B$ and $B \to C$ is rate-determining (C true).

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about nucleophilic aromatic substitution ($\text{S}_\text{N}\text{Ar}$) via the addition–elimination mechanism is/are correct?
optionsEn: Strongly electron-withdrawing groups such as $-\text{NO}_2$ or $-\text{CN}$ located *ortho* or *para* to the leaving group dramatically accelerate the reaction.
The reaction proceeds through a resonance-stabilized anionic cyclohexadienyl intermediate (Meisenheimer complex).
A *meta*-$\text{NO}_2$ group activates an aryl chloride toward $\text{S}_\text{N}\text{Ar}$ to the same extent as a *para*-$\text{NO}_2$ group.
Among halogens, fluoride ($-\text{F}$) is typically the fastest-displaced leaving group in addition-rate-limited $\text{S}_\text{N}\text{Ar}$.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) Correct:** *Ortho*/*para* $-\text{NO}_2$/$-\text{CN}$ groups delocalize the negative charge of the Meisenheimer intermediate by resonance.
- **(B) Correct:** The anionic $\sigma$-complex is the Meisenheimer intermediate.
- **(C) Incorrect:** A *meta*-$\text{NO}_2$ group cannot delocalize the carbanion charge by resonance (only weak $-I$), so it activates far less than *ortho*/*para*-$\text{NO}_2$.
- **(D) Correct:** High electronegativity of $\text{F}$ accelerates the rate-determining addition step.
Hence, **(A), (B), and (D)** are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: The angle between the vectors $\vec{a} = \hat{i} + \hat{j}$ and $\vec{b} = \hat{i} + \hat{k}$ is _______ degrees. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: Using $\cos\theta = \frac{\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}}{|\vec{a}||\vec{b}|} = \frac{1(1) + 1(0) + 0(1)}{\sqrt{2}\cdot\sqrt{2}} = \frac{1}{2}$, we obtain $\theta = 60^\circ$.

questions.questionTextEn: The total number of microstates possible for a $p^2$ electronic configuration is _______.
questions.explanationEn: A $p$-subshell has $2(2l+1) = 6$ spin-orbitals. For $2$ electrons, $W = \binom{6}{2} = \frac{6!}{2!\,4!} = 15$.

questions.questionTextEn: According to Wade's rules, the number of skeletal electron pairs (SEP) in the icosahedral borane anion $[\text{B}_{12}\text{H}_{12}]^{2-}$ is _______.
questions.explanationEn: Each of the $12$ $\text{BH}$ units contributes $2$ skeletal electrons and the $2-$ charge contributes $2$ electrons, giving $24 + 2 = 26$ skeletal electrons, or $26/2 = 13$ skeletal electron pairs ($n + 1$ for $n = 12$, *closo*).

questions.questionTextEn:
Cyclohexene reacts with $\text{CH}_2\text{I}_2$ in the presence of $\text{Zn-Cu}$ couple to yield a bicyclic hydrocarbon. The molecular weight of this product is _______ $\text{g mol}^{-1}$. *(answer in integer)*
[Given: atomic weights $\text{H} = 1$, $\text{C} = 12$]
questions.explanationEn: Simmons–Smith cyclopropanation adds a $\text{CH}_2$ group across the double bond of cyclohexene ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10}$) to give bicyclo$[4.1.0]$heptane (norcarane, $\text{C}_7\text{H}_{12}$). Molecular weight $= 7(12) + 12(1) = 96\text{ g mol}^{-1}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A rigid diatomic molecule has a rotational constant $B = 1.92\text{ cm}^{-1}$. The wavenumber of the $J = 2 \to J = 3$ rotational absorption line is _______ $\text{cm}^{-1}$. *(round off to two decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn: For a rigid rotor, $\tilde{\nu}_{J \to J+1} = 2B(J + 1)$. For $J = 2$, $\tilde{\nu}_{2 \to 3} = 2(1.92)(2 + 1) = 11.52\text{ cm}^{-1}$.

questions.questionTextEn: The number of constitutionally distinct linear tripeptides that can be formed from one molecule each of glycine, alanine, and valine (using each amino acid exactly once) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: The number of distinct linear orderings of $3$ different amino acids (from $N$-terminus to $C$-terminus) is $3! = \mathbf{6}$.

questions.questionTextEn: Among the following six compounds—ethanol, methanol, acetone, pentan-3-one, propan-2-ol, and acetophenone—the number of compounds that give a **positive** iodoform test is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: Positive iodoform test: ethanol, acetone, propan-2-ol, and acetophenone ($4$ compounds). Methanol and pentan-3-one lack the required $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ or $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ motif.

questions.questionTextEn:
The osmotic pressure of a $0.10\text{ M}$ aqueous solution of glucose (a non-electrolyte) at $300\text{ K}$ is _______ $\text{atm}$. *(round off to two decimal places)*
[Given: $R = 0.0821\text{ L atm mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}$]
questions.explanationEn: Using $\Pi = CRT$ with $C = 0.10\text{ mol L}^{-1}$, $R = 0.0821\text{ L atm mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}$, and $T = 300\text{ K}$: $\Pi = 0.10 \times 0.0821 \times 300 = 2.463\text{ atm} \approx 2.46\text{ atm}$.

questions.questionTextEn: The limiting molar ionic conductivity of $\text{K}^+$ in water at $298\text{ K}$ is $7.35 \times 10^{-3}\text{ S m}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$. Taking $F = 96500\text{ C mol}^{-1}$, the ionic mobility of $\text{K}^+$ is $X \times 10^{-8}\text{ m}^2\text{ s}^{-1}\text{ V}^{-1}$, where $X$ is _______. *(round off to two decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn: $u(\text{K}^+) = \frac{\lambda^\circ}{|z|F} = \frac{7.35 \times 10^{-3}}{1 \times 96500} = 7.617 \times 10^{-8}\text{ m}^2\text{ s}^{-1}\text{ V}^{-1} \implies X \approx 7.62$.

questions.questionTextEn: The number of stereoisomers formed upon stereospecific *anti*-addition of $\text{Br}_2$ in $\text{CCl}_4$ to $(Z)$-but-2-ene is _______.
questions.explanationEn: *Anti*-addition of $\text{Br}_2$ via a cyclic bromonium ion to $(Z)$-but-2-ene produces a racemic mixture of $(2R,3R)$-2,3-dibromobutane and $(2S,3S)$-2,3-dibromobutane, i.e., **$2$** stereoisomers.

questions.questionTextEn: In the double-chain amphibole silicate tremolite, $\text{Ca}_2\text{Mg}_5[\text{Si}_4\text{O}_{11}]_2(\text{OH})_2$, the magnitude of the negative charge $|q|$ on each $[\text{Si}_4\text{O}_{11}]^{q-}$ repeat unit is _______.
questions.explanationEn: Each $\text{Si}$ is $+4$ and each $\text{O}$ is $-2$, so $q = 4(+4) + 11(-2) = 16 - 22 = -6$. Consistently, in the neutral mineral formula: $2(+2) + 5(+2) + 2(q) + 2(-1) = 0 \implies 12 + 2q = 0 \implies q = -6$, so $|q| = 6$.

questions.questionTextEn: For the symmetric hexaric (aldaric) acid $\text{HO}_2\text{C–(CHOH)}_4\text{–CO}_2\text{H}$ containing $4$ stereogenic carbons, the number of **optically active** stereoisomers is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: For a symmetric chain with an even number $n = 4$ of stereogenic centers: number of optically active isomers $= 2^{n-1} = 2^3 = 8$ ($4$ enantiomeric pairs), and number of *meso* isomers $= 2^{(n/2)-1} = 2^1 = 2$ (total $= 10$ stereoisomers). Hence there are $8$ optically active stereoisomers.

questions.questionTextEn: The total number of stereoisomers (including enantiomeric pairs) possible for 2-isopropyl-5-methylcyclohexan-1-ol (the menthol family) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: 2-Isopropyl-5-methylcyclohexan-1-ol has $3$ unsymmetrically substituted chiral centers (C1, C2, C5) and no internal symmetry, giving $2^3 = \mathbf{8}$ stereoisomers ($4$ diastereomeric racemic pairs: menthol, neomenthol, isomenthol, and neoisomenthol).

questions.questionTextEn:
Cyclohexanone is treated with ethyl bromoacetate ($\text{BrCH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{Et}$) and activated $\text{Zn}$ dust in $\text{THF}$ (Reformatsky reaction), followed by aqueous workup and dehydration with $p$-toluenesulfonic acid ($\text{TsOH}$, $\Delta$). The molecular weight of the resulting unsaturated ester is _______ $\text{g mol}^{-1}$. *(answer in integer)*
[Given: atomic weights $\text{H} = 1$, $\text{C} = 12$, $\text{O} = 16$]
questions.explanationEn: The Reformatsky reaction of cyclohexanone ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$) with $\text{BrCH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{Et}$ gives ethyl 2-(1-hydroxycyclohexyl)acetate ($\text{C}_{10}\text{H}_{18}\text{O}_3$). Acid-catalyzed dehydration eliminates $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ to yield an unsaturated ester of formula $\text{C}_{10}\text{H}_{16}\text{O}_2$. Molecular weight $= 10(12) + 16(1) + 2(16) = \mathbf{168}\text{ g mol}^{-1}$.

questions.questionTextEn: The $\text{pH}$ of a $0.010\text{ M}$ aqueous solution of a weak monoprotic acid $\text{HA}$ with $K_a = 1.0 \times 10^{-3}$ at $25\,^\circ\text{C}$ (without neglecting dissociation relative to initial concentration) is _______. *(round off to two decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn: Since $K_a/C = 0.10$ is not negligible, solve the exact quadratic $\frac{x^2}{0.010 - x} = 1.0 \times 10^{-3} \implies x^2 + 1.0\times 10^{-3}x - 1.0\times 10^{-5} = 0$. The positive root is $x = [\text{H}^+] = \frac{-10^{-3} + \sqrt{10^{-6} + 4\times 10^{-5}}}{2} = 2.702 \times 10^{-3}\text{ M}$, giving $\text{pH} = -\log_{10}(2.702 \times 10^{-3}) = 2.57$.

questions.questionTextEn:
A $0.500\text{ g}$ sample of a nickel alloy is dissolved and precipitated quantitatively with dimethylglyoxime in ammoniacal medium, yielding $0.2887\text{ g}$ of dry $\text{Ni(dmgH)}_2$. The weight percentage ($\%\text{ w/w}$) of nickel in the alloy is _______ $\%$. *(round off to two decimal places)*

[Given: Atomic mass of $\text{Ni} = 58.69\text{ g mol}^{-1}$; molar mass of $\text{Ni(dmgH)}_2 = 288.69\text{ g mol}^{-1}$]
questions.explanationEn:
Moles of $\text{Ni} = \text{moles of } \text{Ni(dmgH)}_2 = \frac{0.2887}{288.69} = 1.0000 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol}$.
Mass of $\text{Ni} = 1.0000 \times 10^{-3} \times 58.69 = 0.05869\text{ g}$.
Weight percentage of $\text{Ni} = \frac{0.05869}{0.500} \times 100\% = 11.74\%$.

questions.questionTextEn: To maintain a fixed fractional surface coverage $\theta = 0.40$ of a gas on charcoal, the required equilibrium pressure increases from $0.20\text{ bar}$ at $250\text{ K}$ to $0.80\text{ bar}$ at $300\text{ K}$. Using $R = 8.314\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$, the isosteric enthalpy of adsorption $\Delta H_{\text{ads}}$ (with sign) is _______ $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. *(round off to one decimal place)*
questions.explanationEn: By the Clausius–Clapeyron relation at constant $\theta$, $\ln\left(\frac{P_2}{P_1}\right) = \frac{-\Delta H_{\text{ads}}}{R}\left(\frac{1}{T_1} - \frac{1}{T_2}\right)$. Thus $\Delta H_{\text{ads}} = -\frac{8.314 \times \ln 4}{(1/250 - 1/300)} = -17288\text{ J mol}^{-1} = -17.29\text{ kJ mol}^{-1} \approx -17.3\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

questions.questionTextEn: For a reaction with a temperature-independent enthalpy change $\Delta_r H^\circ = -50.0\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, the standard Gibbs free energy change at $300\text{ K}$ is $\Delta_r G^\circ = -20.0\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$. Using the Gibbs–Helmholtz equation, the value of $\Delta_r G^\circ$ at $400\text{ K}$ is _______ $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. *(round off to one decimal place)*
questions.explanationEn: Integrating the Gibbs–Helmholtz equation for constant $\Delta_r H^\circ$ gives $\frac{\Delta_r G_2^\circ}{T_2} - \frac{\Delta_r G_1^\circ}{T_1} = \Delta_r H^\circ\left(\frac{1}{T_2} - \frac{1}{T_1}\right)$. Substituting values: $\frac{\Delta_r G_2^\circ}{400} = \frac{-20.0}{300} + (-50.0)\left(\frac{1}{400} - \frac{1}{300}\right) = -0.06667 + 0.04167 = -0.0250\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}$. Multiplying by $400\text{ K}$ yields $\Delta_r G_2^\circ = -10.0\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

questions.questionTextEn:
Toluene is converted via the following sequence: (i) mononitration with $\text{HNO}_3/\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ (separating the major *para* isomer); (ii) oxidation with hot alkaline $\text{KMnO}_4$ followed by acidification; (iii) reduction with $\text{Sn/HCl}$ followed by careful neutralization to the neutral amino acid (PABA). The molecular weight of the final product is _______ $\text{g mol}^{-1}$. *(answer in integer)*
[Given: atomic weights $\text{H} = 1$, $\text{C} = 12$, $\text{N} = 14$, $\text{O} = 16$]
questions.explanationEn: The sequence yields 4-nitrotoluene $\to$ 4-nitrobenzoic acid $\to$ 4-aminobenzoic acid (PABA, $\text{H}_2\text{N}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, formula $\text{C}_7\text{H}_7\text{NO}_2$). Molecular weight $= 7(12) + 7(1) + 14 + 2(16) = \mathbf{137}\text{ g mol}^{-1}$.

questions.questionTextEn: The scalar projection of the vector $\vec{A} = 7\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - \hat{k}$ along the direction of $\vec{B} = 2\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: The scalar projection is $\frac{\vec{A}\cdot\vec{B}}{|\vec{B}|}$. Here $\vec{A}\cdot\vec{B} = 7(2) + 2(-2) + (-1)(1) = 14 - 4 - 1 = 9$, and $|\vec{B}| = \sqrt{2^2 + (-2)^2 + 1^2} = \sqrt{9} = 3$. Thus the scalar projection is $\frac{9}{3} = 3$.
